title: Be a person
hookLine: Hillel: where no one is being a person, strive to be one (Pirkei Avot 2:5)
tomorrow: who's actually wise: the one who knows most, or someone else?

lines: WHERE NO ONE IS BEING A PERSON...
cards: A bag splits on a crowded train and oranges roll everywhere. Twenty people see it. Each one waits for someone else.
Hillel has a line for that exact room. In Pirkei Avot he says: in a place where there are no people, strive to be a person. He doesn't mean an empty room.
He means a full room where nobody is acting like one. The Hebrew word is ish, a person, a man. In Yiddish, that kind of person is a mensch.

teach.h: A HORSE, A SERVANT, A LOST FORTUNE.
teach.b: The Talmud tells how Hillel lived it. There was a man from a good family who had lost everything.

The Torah says to lend a poor person sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth, and this man had been used to riding a horse with a servant running ahead. So Hillel got him a horse and a servant.
One day there was no servant to be found.
So Hillel, the great sage, ran ahead of the horse himself. That's the teaching. In Judaism, being a mensch isn't a personality trait.
It's an obligation, and it includes a person's dignity, not only their bread. And when no one else steps up, the obligation lands on you. Now a neighbor who says something close.
In the Gospel of Luke, Jesus tells of a man beaten by thieves and left on the road. A priest passes by on the other side. So does a Levite.
A Samaritan stops, binds his wounds, and pays for his care. Jesus asks who was neighbor to the man, and says, in the King James words, "Go, and do thou likewise."
Shared: in a place where no one is being a person, one person is. The honest difference: Hillel's saying is about the room you're standing in.
Luke's parable answers a lawyer's question, who is my neighbor, and makes a Samaritan the one who shows it; Christians read it as Jesus' teaching on love of neighbor.

how: Jews study Hillel's saying in Pirkei Avot; being a mensch, a decent person who steps up, is a common Jewish ideal, and Christians read the Good Samaritan in Luke 10 as a teaching on loving one's neighbor.

o: stand out from the crowd so others notice you
act like a grown-up and stop being so playful
step up and act decently when no one else will

games.q: who stepped up: tap the pairs.
p: ran ahead of the horse himself
passed by on the other side

s: 'where there are no people' means when you're alone in an empty room
Hillel means a place where no one is acting like a person: a full room, and nobody stepping up.
the Talmud says Hillel himself ran ahead of a poor man's horse
when no servant could be found, Hillel ran ahead himself, giving the man back his dignity.
in Luke, Jesus is the one who asks 'who is my neighbor?'
a lawyer asks it; Jesus answers with the parable and ends by asking which one was neighbor to the man.

games.q: group project: the deadline's tomorrow and three people have gone silent in the chat. what's Hillel's move?
o: where no one is acting like a person, be one: pick up a piece and say so kindly.
wait it out; if nobody does it, it isn't really your job either.
post a call-out naming who did nothing, so everyone sees it.
games.why: Hillel's line puts the obligation on whoever's left. and the horse story says do it with dignity, not a call-out.

practice: Take out your phone and think of one person others might have left out lately: someone sick, someone new, someone who went quiet.
Write them a short, plain message, no big speech, just that you thought of them, and send it if it feels right.

wordCard.voice: Be a person: Hillel's charge, where no one is acting like a person, strive to be one.
